user.title: Connect to your PLC
user.description: Choose a PLC found on your network, or enter its address yourself.

manual.title: Connect to your PLC
manual.description: Enter the address of the PLC. The automatic search only finds PLCs on the same network as Home Assistant.

data_description.host: IP address or host name, for example 192.168.1.50.

data_description.port: UDP port of the PLC. Default 61682.
data_description.local_port: UDP port Home Assistant sends from. Default 61681; 0 lets the system choose.

discovery_confirm.title: Add this PLC?
discovery_confirm.description:
{ident} at {host}.

Home Assistant will read its modules and variable names.

upload.title: Upload the .pub file
upload.description:
Upload the `.pub` file that belongs to the program running in the PLC. A `.piz` or `.zip` that contains it works too.

Mosaic writes the file into the project folder when it compiles the program, provided Project manager → Sw → Export files → Assembler (.pub) is enabled.

no_map.title: This PLC stores no variable names
no_map.description:
{modules} modules were found, but this PLC does not store its program's `.pub` file, the list of the program's variables. Without it, Home Assistant:

- **cannot switch anything.** It only shows states: what is on, temperatures, button presses.
- **does not know your names.** Everything is named by module type and bus address.

You can also add the file later under Configure: entities created now keep their history, get your names, and control is added.

menu_option_descriptions.upload: Your own names and control from the start.
menu_option_descriptions.inventory_only: States only for now. Add the file later under Configure.

busy.title: The PLC is in use
busy.description: Another program is connected to the PLC, for example the programming tool, and the variable names cannot be read meanwhile. Close it, then try again.

file_no_match.title: The file matches none of the modules
file_no_match.description: {modules} modules were found, but no variable in the file belongs to any of them. It is most likely the `.pub` of another project.

menu_option_descriptions.use_file: Home Assistant will only show states, under generic names, and cannot switch anything. The file's variables are kept and included in diagnostics, which helps add support for programs with their own naming.

reconfigure.title: Change the PLC connection
reconfigure.description: Change how Home Assistant reaches the PLC. The stored variable names are kept; to refresh them use Configure → Reload variable names from the PLC.

speed.title: Update speed
speed.description: Measured now: a full read of {values} values takes about {read_ms} ms. With the pause below, each of them is refreshed about every {cycle_ms} ms. Saving reloads the integration.

data.fast_scan_interval: Read buttons and motion sensors every (ms)

data_description.scan_interval: Default 500; 0 starts the next read immediately. A shorter pause gives faster updates but more traffic to the PLC.
data_description.fast_scan_interval: The {fast_inputs} on/off inputs (wall buttons, motion sensors, contacts) are read separately on their own short cycle, so a quick press is not missed between full reads. 100 is recommended; 0 turns this off.

speed_unmeasured.title: Update speed
speed_unmeasured.description: How often Home Assistant reads values from the PLC. Saving reloads the integration.

data.fast_scan_interval: Read buttons and motion sensors every (ms)

data_description.scan_interval: Default 500; 0 starts the next read immediately. A shorter pause gives faster updates but more traffic to the PLC.
data_description.fast_scan_interval: On/off inputs (wall buttons, motion sensors, contacts) are read separately on their own short cycle, so a quick press is not missed between full reads. 100 is recommended; 0 turns this off.

diagnostics.title: Download diagnostics
diagnostics.description: The diagnostics file describes the PLC's modules and variables. Attach it when you report a problem or ask for a module to be supported.

data_description.anonymize_diagnostics: Replaces the words in your variable names (rooms, people…) with placeholders such as w1, w2, so the file can be shared publicly. Words the integration relies on (light, plug, pir, magnet, ON/OFF…) and module codes are kept. The choice is remembered, also for ⋮ → Download diagnostics.

map_changed.title: EPSNET: PLC program changed
map_changed.description: The variable names stored in the PLC changed since they were last loaded ({points} variables now, checksum {old_crc} → {new_crc}). The new names have been applied. Review your entities and automations in case variables moved.

unsupported_modules.title: EPSNET: PLC modules not supported yet
unsupported_modules.description: {count} module(s) on the PLC bus are not supported yet ({codes}), so they have no entities. To help add them, open the integration, choose Configure → Download diagnostics and attach the file to an issue at {issue_url}. Variable names are hidden in the file unless you choose otherwise.

no_variable_map.title: EPSNET: no variable names
no_variable_map.description: This entry has no variable names, so its {count} module(s) are listed without entities: without the names it is unknown where their data sits and how to switch them. Open the integration and choose Configure → Reload variable names from the PLC, or Load variable names from a .pub file.

no_variable_map_read_only.title: EPSNET: no .pub file — states only, no control
no_variable_map_read_only.description: The PLC program's .pub file is missing, so Home Assistant only shows the states of this PLC's {count} module(s) and cannot switch anything. Entities are named by module type and bus address. To control lights and sockets and get your own names, open the integration and choose Configure → Load variable names from a .pub file (or Reload variable names from the PLC, if the file is stored there now). Entities keep their history.

program_changed.title: EPSNET: PLC program changed
program_changed.description: A new program was sent to the PLC, and its input/output layout could not be read again (the PLC may still be busy with the programming tool). Module channels placed from the program are unavailable until then. Reload the integration to try again.
